title: Form UX Timing
summary: This reel explains the importance of timing in form validation, demonstrating why validating on blur is superior to validating on submit or on every keystroke.

transcript.text: The error fires while you're still typing.
The timing is the whole thing.
Validate only on submit and they fill 10 fields blind.
Hit the button and everything turns red at once.
Now they're scrolling up, hunting for what went wrong.
Validate on every keystroke and you punish them mid-word.
They type the first letter, you scream "invalid email".
Validate on blur. Wait until they leave the field, then check it.
They've finished the thought, so the feedback lands as helpful, not nagging.
Once a field is wrong, the rules change.
Switch that one to live and clear the error the instant they fix it.
Don't make them submit again to find out they're forgiven.
A green check is feedback too.
Confirm the field is right, don't only flag wrong.
Silence after effort feels like the form is judging them.
Follow for more form UX. Save this for your next build.

on_screen_text: ON SUBMIT: Errors all at once
ON KEYSTROKE: Wrong before they finish
ON BLUR: Check when they leave
AFTER AN ERROR: Then escalate to live
ON SUCCESS: Confirm it, don't just flag wrong
Silence feels judged. Confirm feels safe.
FORM UX - TIMING: Timing is the UX.
design_principles: Avoid 'On Submit' validation to prevent overwhelming users with errors.
Avoid 'On Keystroke' validation for initial entry to prevent premature error messages.
Use 'On Blur' validation to provide feedback after a user completes a field.
Switch to live validation only after an error is detected to provide immediate resolution feedback.
Provide positive reinforcement with success states.
before_after: Contrasts the frustration of 'On Submit' and 'On Keystroke' validation with the smoother experience of 'On Blur' and 'Live on Error' validation.
